answer: Each agent may trade only through a bonded account: it locks a scarce token before acting, and counterparties can claim that bond when a signed delivery receipt proves the agent broke an agreed rule. A cipher links each receipt to the account without exposing its owner, while a trellis of reputation records upheld claims across markets. Spawning identities no longer multiplies influence: every one needs capital, and a gale of disposable accounts risks forfeiting it.
